findings.issue: The commit under review (7d1421b4) printed five unmasked phone numbers into the dated evidence doc, breaking both the doc's own stated rule and FEAT-002's acceptance criterion 'The doc contains no credential value and no full phone number'. Line 27 asserts '**Phone numbers in this document are masked to the last four digits**, per the repo's logging rule', and the main reproduction table at lines 188-200 honours it by masking to the last four with the digit COUNT stated separately - which is where the mechanism actually lives, since the legacy corruption fired when country code + national == 10 digits. The iteration-3 section added at lines 318-320, 333 and 336 does not: it prints '+919330994400' three times, '+6591234567', '91933099440<U+0660>' and '91<U+00B2>09330994400'. Measured per revision, scanning for runs of 7+ digits and discarding the account id, the GitHub run ids and the date stamps: f8a73fb0 [], ac1b0c37 [], ed9fa198 [], 892e2d63 [], 7d1421b4 ['09330994400', '6591234567', '91234567', '91933099440', '919330994400']. So this is a regression introduced by this commit, not an inherited condition, which is also why iteration 3's scan of the same doc reported only account ids and CI run ids. '919330994400' is not a fixture: amplify/functions/shared/lambda_utils/notifications/events.py:98 sets _DEFAULT_BUSINESS_NUMBERS = '+919330994400,+919903300044,+918031830030' and line 95 records it as WABA1 / primary WhatsApp Calling, so a live business number is now in a committed doc. Disclosure harm is low because a business number is public-facing; what makes it blocking is that the constraint was explicit, the doc asserts compliance with it two paragraphs in, and 892e2d63 deliberately rewrote a sentence to avoid printing two Singapore spellings. A doc that states a masking rule and then breaks it teaches the next reader that the rule is decorative.
findings.required_change: Mask the five numbers to the last four digits with the digit count stated separately, matching the format already used at lines 188-200 (e.g. '+65 ···<U+00B2>···4567' with '10 digits' beside it, '+91 ···4400<U+00B2>' with '12 digits', '+91 ···<U+00B2>0···4400' with '13 digits'). Nothing is lost: the superscript rows carry their meaning in the POSITION of the non-decimal character, and the trunk-zero row's point is only that the superscript sits between the '91' and the '0'. Leave tests/test_phone_country_code_preservation.py alone - a case table has to be literal to be assertable, and tests are not the artefact the rule governs. After the edit, re-run the scan for runs of 7+ digits over the doc and confirm the only remaining hits are the account id, the GitHub run ids and the date stamps, as every earlier revision showed. No source change is needed; the predicate and ASCII fixes themselves are correct and verified.
